[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Iron Mountain facility is part of the company data center business, which traces to a December 2017 purchase of IO Data Centers United States division for 1.3 billion dollars, acquiring four colocation data centers in New Jersey, Ohio, and Arizona, though this specific Virginia or Illinois location was not confirmed as part of that transaction in available sourcing this session. Iron Mountain itself was founded in 1951 as Iron Mountain Atomic Storage Corporation by Herman Knaust, a former mushroom entrepreneur who had purchased a depleted iron ore mine near Kingston, New York, went public in 1996, became a real estate investment trust in 2014, and as of 2023 is headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The operators own current data center locations page describes its Northern Virginia presence as 400 plus MW across 142 acres in Manassas, and its own VA-1 and VA-2 solution guides separately describe an 83 acre campus that is the first of four planned campus data centers growing toward a nine facility, two million plus square foot development, confirming this is a real, large, multi building campus consistent with this registrys six separately numbered VA rows. This session resolved a street address for this specific VA-1 row. The operators own VA-1 solution guide confirms an 83 acre campus, 168,000 square feet, and 12.4 MW, Uptime Tier III certified, but does not itself publish a street number. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned 11680 Hayden Rd, Manassas, VA 20109 at 0.9 confidence. Three sibling VA rows in this same batch independently geocoded to the same street with a coherent, evenly spaced building number sequence, 11600, 11640, 11680, consistent with a real, sequentially developed multi building campus matching the operators own description, and this cross row internal consistency is treated here as the corroborating check in place of a named press or aggregator source, which this session did not find. Given this, the session applies 11680 Hayden Rd as this rows address, flagged for a future researcher to confirm against a named source if one becomes available.

reading.body:
Iron Mountain VA-1 is a single building within a larger 83-acre multi-building campus in Manassas, Virginia, with 12.4 MW of published IT capacity and 168,000 square feet. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this 12.4 MW represents roughly 310 racks, an order of magnitude smaller than hyperscaler campuses but substantial for a colocation facility. The campus holds Uptime Tier III certification, which qualifies it for enterprises requiring 99.99% availability but does not indicate specialized capability for the highest-density GPU workloads.

Virginia's published data center capacity stands at 1,375 MW across 23 facilities that report figures. Iron Mountain VA-1 ranks 24th in the state, meaning 23 other facilities publish larger capacities. However, Virginia has 326 mapped facilities with no published capacity, so the actual state total is unknown. The presence of multiple Iron Mountain VA buildings suggests the operator is developing this Manassas site as a significant regional cluster, with the company's own materials describing a longer-term build toward nine facilities and two million square feet across the county.

This facility's relevance to AI scaling depends on whether its colocation model and Tier III availability meet tenant requirements. The 12.4 MW here is an order of magnitude smaller than individual hyperscaler data center modules and carries no published certifications for GPU density, cooling capability, or power distribution redundancy specific to AI workloads. The broader Manassas campus may matter if Iron Mountain develops adjacent buildings with higher IT capacity and AI-grade infrastructure, but published specifications for those buildings are not available.
